name: Tethercam
tagline: Your iPhone as a Windows or Linux webcam over USB, or Wi-Fi once paired, at up to 4K.
summary: Tethercam turns an iPhone into a standard webcam on Windows 11 and Linux that Teams, Zoom, OBS, Streamlabs and browsers can use. The phone hardware-encodes H.264 and the PC decodes it on the GPU. On Windows, a virtual camera hands it to any app; on Linux, a v4l2loopback device does. No account, no watermark: plug in the cable and pick the camera. Pair once over the cable to use it over Wi-Fi, encrypted end to end.
role: Solo: design, Windows and Linux (C++), iOS (Swift), CI/CD

highlights.title: Full resolution
highlights.text: Every format the phone's lenses offer, up to 3840×2160 at 60 fps, exposed as standard webcam formats.

highlights.title: USB first, Wi-Fi optional
highlights.text: Video travels through Apple's USB tunnel, ~100 ms glass-to-glass at 1080p30. Pair once over the cable and it also works over Wi-Fi, encrypted with Noise; nothing leaves the local network.

highlights.title: A real virtual camera
highlights.text: A Frame Server media source registered with MFCreateVirtualCamera, so it works in every Windows 11 camera app.

highlights.title: Windows and Linux
highlights.text: The same shared C++ core drives both hosts: a Frame Server virtual camera on Windows, a v4l2loopback camera with VA-API decode on Linux; shipped as .msi, .deb and .rpm.

highlights.title: Built for streaming
highlights.text: A local status API lets stream overlays hide the camera while the phone is offline.
